projectReview.overallStatus: Good with minor fixes required before production deployment

architectAgent.status: Good - well-structured architecture with minor improvements needed
strengths: Clean separation of concerns with store/, components/, pages/, utils/ directories
Zustand stores are well-designed with clear separation (auth, project, builder)
Component registry pattern enables extensible section system
Undo/redo system implemented via history stack in builder store
Auto-save mechanism built into builder page lifecycle
Firebase Functions architecture follows callable pattern for secure API access
Multi-tenant Firestore security rules with role-based access
issues: Drag-and-drop is click-based (add from sidebar) rather than true HTML5 DnD via @dnd-kit
No code-splitting or lazy loading for section components
No error boundaries implemented for component rendering
Firebase config uses hardcoded fallback strings instead of failing fast when env vars are missing
No TypeScript usage for type safety across the codebase
recommendations: Implement @dnd-kit DndContext for true drag-and-drop reordering on canvas
Add React.lazy() and Suspense for section component code-splitting
Add ErrorBoundary wrapper around Renderer component
Remove hardcoded fallback values in firebase.js, throw on missing env vars
Consider migrating to TypeScript for better maintainability at scale

architectureReview.frontendStructure: Well-organized Vite + React 19 project with domain-based component folders. Pages handle routing, components handle rendering, stores manage state. Clean separation.
architectureReview.backendStructure: Solid Firebase Cloud Functions implementation with 7 endpoints. Admin SDK initialized correctly. Missing input validation on function parameters and no rate limiting.
architectureReview.firebaseStructure: Firestore schema follows users->projects->versions hierarchy. Security rules enforce multi-tenant isolation. Indexes configured for primary queries. Compound indexes could be improved for advanced filtering.
architectureReview.rendererSystem: Excellent component registry pattern. JSON-to-React mapping is clean and extensible. Renderer gracefully handles unknown component types with fallback UI.
architectureReview.componentSystem: 12 reusable section components with consistent prop interfaces. Good use of default props. Props editing in PropertiesPanel varies by component type. Some components could be more granular.
architectureReview.scalability: Firebase architecture scales horizontally. Zustand avoids Redux boilerplate. Missing caching layer for Firestore reads. No pagination for project list (could be issue at scale). AI generation uses mock fallback which is good for dev but needs production hardening.

qaAgent.status: Good UI/UX quality with accessibility and SEO gaps

Responsive preview modes (desktop, tablet, mobile) implemented
Builder layout with sidebar, canvas, and properties panel
Section components render correctly with default props
Template marketplace displays and filters correctly
Project CRUD operations working in dashboard
Publish dialog UI complete with custom domain support
All 12 section components render without errors

No keyboard navigation support for drag-and-drop section reordering
No image alt text validation in gallery section
No form validation feedback in contact section form

qualityReview.responsiveDesign: Three preview modes implemented. Canvas correctly constrains width per mode. All section components use responsive Tailwind classes. Good foundation but mobile-specific layouts not tested.
qualityReview.uiConsistency: Consistent use of indigo color palette, rounded corners, and spacing. Buttons share consistent styles. Modal, Input, and LoadingSpinner components follow same design language.
qualityReview.contentValidation: No input validation on contact form. No character limits on text fields in PropertiesPanel. AI-generated content has no quality filtering.
qualityReview.seoValidation: Basic SEO fields (title, description, ogImage) in project settings. No meta tag generation in preview/published output. No sitemap generation.
qualityReview.accessibility: Limited ARIA attributes. Color contrast not verified. No skip-navigation links. No focus management in builder modals. Keyboard navigation partially supported.
qualityReview.performance: Bundle size at 669KB JS + 39KB CSS is reasonable. No lazy loading for section components. Firestore reads are unbatched. No image optimization pipeline.

deploymentAgent.status: Near-ready - requires Firebase configuration and environment setup

deploymentChecks.firebaseHosting: firebase.json configured with rewrite rules for SPA routing. Public directory set to dist/. Emulator config present for local development.
deploymentChecks.environmentVariables: 7 env vars defined in .env.example. Firebase config uses import.meta.env.VITE_* pattern. No runtime validation. GEMINI_API_KEY only in functions/ backend.
deploymentChecks.buildOptimization: Vite build successful (459ms). Output: 669KB JS + 39KB CSS. No minification issues. Source maps disabled in production. Chunk size warning indicates opportunity for code-splitting.
deploymentChecks.securityRules: Firestore rules enforce user isolation via isOwner() helper. Role-based admin access. Published sites are publicly readable. Default deny catch-all rule in place. no storage rules were created (only storage.rules with basic auth check).
deploymentChecks.apiSafety: Firebase Functions use onCall pattern (auto-auth). No input sanitization. No rate limiting. No request size validation. Mock fallback in AI function could be exploited in production.
deploymentChecks.domainReadiness: Custom domain field in publish dialog. Default project-id.webforge-ai.web.app URL generation. No DNS verification logic. No SSL certificate automation.

issues: Firebase project credentials are placeholders - deployment will fail until .env is configured

Configure GitHub Actions for automated deployment workflow
